name: codeflare
description: AI coding assistant for local (OpenAI-compatible), OpenAI, and Claude backends

commands.title: CodeFlare: Prove It (independently verify the last change)
CodeFlare: Break My Solution (adversarial pass on the last change)
CodeFlare: Add API Key for an External Service
CodeFlare: Remove External Service API Key

enumDescriptions: Anthropic Claude API (api.anthropic.com, native Messages API)
codeflare.provider.description: Which backend to talk to. Determines the API endpoint, auth header, and request format.

codeflare.endpoint.description: API base URL. Leave blank to use the provider default (local: http://localhost:8001, openai: https://api.openai.com, anthropic: https://api.anthropic.com).

codeflare.model.description: Model name/ID. Leave blank to auto-discover it from the server (local provider: the model served on /v1/models) or, for OpenAI/Anthropic, use the provider default (openai: gpt-4o, anthropic: claude-opus-4-8). A value here always overrides discovery.

codeflare.autoDetectModel.description: When the model field is blank and the provider is local, query the server's /v1/models and use the model it serves — so the model name never has to be typed. An explicit model setting always takes precedence.

codeflare.maxTokens.description: Maximum response tokens. 0 = auto: scale to the detected context window (n_ctx minus the prompt), capped at 65536 to avoid runaway output. Set a positive number to use that as a fixed ceiling instead (still bounded by what fits in the window).

codeflare.contextLines.description: Lines of context around selection to include

codeflare.maxContextFiles.description: Maximum number of open files to include as context

codeflare.maxContextChars.description: Maximum total characters of context to send

codeflare.agentMode.description: Let the model explore the workspace with file tools (list_files, read_file, search_text)

codeflare.agentMaxSteps.description: Maximum number of tool-calling steps the agent may take per message (higher = can build larger things in one go)

codeflare.agentEdit.description: Allow the agent to create and edit files by path (create_file, edit_file)

codeflare.confirmEdits.description: Show a diff and ask for confirmation before the agent writes any file. When off, edits are applied directly (like the Claude plugin).

codeflare.editSearchMaxLines.description: Maximum number of lines an edit_file SEARCH block may span. Keeps the agent making small targeted edits instead of regenerating whole files.

codeflare.overwriteMaxLines.description: Maximum size (in lines) of an existing file that create_file may overwrite. Larger files must be changed with edit_file.

codeflare.agentRunCommands.description: Allow the agent to run shell commands (tests, build, git) and read their output

codeflare.agentProbes.description: Allow the agent to place temporary measurement probes in your code (one-line instrumentation) to see what happens at runtime, then read the values back. Probes report to stdout and to .codeflare/probes.jsonl. Requires agentEdit.

codeflare.probeAutoStrip.description: Remove every probe again at the end of the turn that placed it, so instrumentation never stays in your code. Turn this off to measure across several turns — e.g. a server that keeps running — and remove the probes yourself afterwards.

codeflare.agentDebug.description: BETA: give the agent debugger tools (set breakpoints, start debugging via the project's launch.json, continue/step, read the call stack and variables, evaluate expressions) so it can investigate a runtime bug in the real debugger instead of adding temporary logging. Off by default because it adds several tools to every prompt; turn it on when you want the agent to debug. Requires agentRunCommands (debugging executes the program).

codeflare.pentestMode.description: Penetration-testing mode. Tells the agent it is operating under an authorized, in-scope engagement so it actively carries out security tests (recon, scanning, fuzzing, exploitation, payload/PoC generation) instead of hedging, adding disclaimers, or refusing. Off by default so ordinary coding gets a clean reasoning environment; enable it explicitly only for assets you own or are contracted to assess.

codeflare.confirmCommands.description: Ask for confirmation before the agent runs a shell command (except trusted ones below)

codeflare.trustedCommands.description: EXTRA command prefixes that run without a confirmation prompt, merged with the built-in safe list (mkdir, node, python, npm, git status, godot, …) — the built-ins always apply. Every part of a chained command (split on && || & ; |, quotes respected) must match; a leading 'cd <dir>' and a leading './' or '.\' (run-from-here) are handled. An entry containing '*' is a glob — use it for version-embedded executables, e.g. 'godot_v*' matches 'Godot_v4.7.1-stable_win64.exe'.

codeflare.artifactRoots.description: Extra folders the agent may READ from (never write) — for program OUTPUT that lands outside the workspace, e.g. a game/app's user-data dir. The OS temp dir is always readable; add appdata-style locations here. Supports env vars (%APPDATA%, ${HOME}) and ~ . Examples: "%APPDATA%\\Godot\\app_userdata", "%LOCALAPPDATA%\\MyApp", "~/.local/share/MyApp". SECURITY: appdata can hold tokens/cookies; with web access on, read access there is an exfiltration surface — only add roots you trust. Mutating tools stay workspace-only regardless.

codeflare.commandTimeout.description: Timeout in milliseconds for agent-run shell commands

codeflare.diagnosticsLoop.description: After the agent edits files, check them for editor errors and automatically ask the agent to fix them

codeflare.diagnosticsMaxRounds.description: Maximum automatic fix rounds triggered by the diagnostics loop and the verify gate

codeflare.verifyGate.description: After the agent finishes editing, automatically verify the project and feed any failure back so the agent fixes it before declaring done. This runs a verify command (see codeflare.verifyCommand — auto-detected when blank: a typecheck via 'npm run typecheck' or 'npx tsc --noEmit') and also reports NEW errors the changes introduced in files the agent did not touch (regressions). Requires agentRunCommands for the command step.

codeflare.verifyCommand.description: Command run by the verify gate after edits (e.g. 'npm run typecheck', 'npm test', or 'npm run typecheck && npm test'). Leave blank to auto-select per stack: CodeFlare detects the project's stacks (per module) and runs the cheapest sound check (typecheck/syntax/build) for each module whose files changed, using the project's own commands. Its output is fed back to the agent when it fails. Runs without a confirmation prompt — you set it yourself.

codeflare.verifyTimeout.description: Timeout in milliseconds for the verify-gate command (typecheck/tests can be slower than ordinary commands).

codeflare.diffReview.description: Before the agent finishes a turn that changed files, have it review its OWN diff against your request as a REQUIREMENT check — for each thing you asked for, does the diff actually satisfy what it MEANS (not a convenient reinterpretation)? 'Self-review passed' only appears when every requirement is met with evidence; unmet ones are fed back for a bounded fix round, and if the fix rounds run out, the still-unmet requirements are surfaced to you instead of silently declaring done. Runs after diagnostics and the verify gate pass, so it focuses on requirements and scope, not syntax.

codeflare.clarifyAmbiguity.description: When a request hinges on a domain concept that does NOT exist anywhere in the codebase (e.g. asking to open a 'project' in an app that has no notion of a project), let the agent ask ONE concise clarifying question before planning instead of silently guessing an interpretation. CodeFlare also injects a note listing request terms it could not find in the code, so the model has the evidence to decide. Only fires for a central, genuinely absent concept — not minor details. Turn off if you never want clarifying questions.

codeflare.repoMap.description: Inject a compact project map (each source file with its top-level definitions) into the model's context, and offer the find_related tool. Helps the model reuse existing code and match the codebase's conventions instead of reinventing them. Rebuilt as files change; bounded in size.

codeflare.metrics.description: Record one line of metrics per turn to .codeflare/metrics.jsonl (model, tool-call count, edit failures, verify failures, diagnostics errors, human interventions, tokens, files changed, outcome, duration). Groundwork for benchmarking models against the same task. Local only; .codeflare is hidden from the agent and excluded from the VSIX.

codeflare.planApproval.description: When the agent creates a plan for a multi-step task, pause and let you review it (approve or give remarks) before it starts executing

codeflare.visualVerify.description: Offer the verify_visual tool: the agent produces a screenshot (a web page via Playwright, a plot via savefig, a game/app via its own screenshot) and asks the model to check it against the intended result, feeding back concrete visual differences. Requires a VISION-capable model on your endpoint (it sends the image to /v1/chat/completions as an image part). Turn off if your model can't see images.

codeflare.blenderPath.markdownDescription: Where Blender is installed, for headless 3D/STL generation. Accepts the install folder (`C:\Program Files\Blender Foundation\Blender 5.1`), its parent (`C:\Program Files\Blender Foundation` — the newest version wins), or the executable itself. Leave empty to look for `blender` on PATH.

codeflare.imageQC.description: Pixel-check PNGs the agent generates (black/empty detection) and automatically feed problems back — with the image attached — so the agent fixes its generation script

codeflare.meshQC.description: Geometrically check STL meshes the agent generates (empty, truncated, collapsed or all-degenerate geometry) and feed problems back with the measured triangle count, bounding box and watertightness so the agent fixes its generation script

codeflare.contextCompaction.description: Trim token overhead from the conversation sent to the model: collapse superseded/duplicate file reads and reads made stale by later edits (structure preserved)

codeflare.contextAutoCompact.description: When the conversation grows large, summarize older turns into a compact note and keep recent turns verbatim (like Claude Code's context compaction)

codeflare.contextCompactThreshold.description: Conversation size in characters above which auto-compaction runs

codeflare.contextKeepRecent.description: How many of the most recent messages to keep verbatim when compacting

codeflare.webAccess.description: Allow the agent to fetch web pages and run web searches (web_fetch, web_search)

codeflare.streamIdleTimeout.description: Abort a request if the server sends nothing for this many milliseconds (stalled-connection watchdog). Also caps context-compaction requests.

codeflare.serverMaxLifetime.description: Automatically stop dev servers the agent started after this many minutes (they otherwise pile up as stray python/node processes holding ports and folders). 0 = never auto-stop. Servers are also stopped when replaced on the same port, via 'CodeFlare: Stop Agent Servers', and on window close.

enumDescriptions: Default. Today's behaviour: confirmation prompts, no hard change budgets.
Opt-in unattended mode with TIGHT limits: max 3 changed files / 250 added lines per turn, protected paths blocked, no publish/deploy/push/installs, untrusted commands refused instead of prompted.
Opt-in unattended mode with wider limits (8 files / 800 added lines). Same hard blocks as conservative.
codeflare.autonomyProfile.description: Deterministic autonomy policy. Non-interactive profiles enforce hard change budgets and path rules at tool level — the model cannot negotiate past them, and anything that would need a confirmation prompt is refused instead. Keep 'interactive' for normal use.

codeflare.allowedPaths.description: Autonomous modes only: when non-empty, the agent may ONLY modify paths matching these globs (e.g. "src/**", "tests/**"). Interactive mode ignores this list.

codeflare.protectedPaths.description: EXTRA protected paths, merged with the built-in defaults (package manifests, lockfiles, .github/**, deployment/**, .env*, keys). In autonomous modes these are blocked outright; interactive mode keeps its normal confirmation behaviour.

codeflare.forbiddenPaths.description: EXTRA forbidden paths, merged with the built-in defaults (**/.ssh/**, credentials, secrets, .git/**, .codeflare/**). Never writable by the agent in ANY mode.

codeflare.changeBudget.description: Per-field overrides on the active profile's change budget (0 = unlimited). Fields: maxChangedFiles, maxNewFiles, maxAddedLines, maxDeletedLines, maxToolCalls, maxWallTimeMs. Exceeding a budget stops the turn with CHANGE_BUDGET_EXCEEDED.

codeflare.mcpServers.description: MCP servers to connect (BETA). Map of name → { command, args, env }. Their tools become available to the agent as mcp__<name>__<tool>.
